grades.quote: When there are no more bytes to read, read returns zero to indicate the end of the file.
grades.reason: Only limited background: it says read returns zero at end of file and that file descriptors cover pipes. It never says a pipe reader sees EOF only after every write end is closed, including the parent's copy. That is the missing diagnosis for the query.
It covers offset sharing through fork/dup and shell redirection with 2>&1. It says nothing about pipe EOF or about unclosed write ends keeping a reader blocked.
It is a POSIX example of closing stdout in a child and reopening a file before exec. It does not cover pipes, EOF, or why a pipe reader never sees EOF.
It is a figure about overlapping locks to avoid lost wake-ups in sleep/wakeup. It does not explain EOF or the write-end-open condition that keeps a pipe reader from getting EOF.
